label: Eventing Storage (Function metadata keyspace)
type: the bucket/scope/collection a Function is configured to use as a scratchpad for its own runtime state (checkpoints, Timer store) - as distinct from eventing:listen-to-location (the mutation source it watches) and eventing:bucket-alias-binding (a data-plane access grant the handler code itself uses). A REQUIRED Function setting, not optional.
recurrence_note: 17 files, shared-source discounted to 13 independent (cross-product duplication upheld on part of the count; the bar is cleared either way).
evidence: Eventing Storage | A bucket, scope, and collection currently defined on your cluster and where you want to store system data for your Eventing Function. This is the Function's metadata bucket.
Eventing Storage, or the Eventing metadata: a collection used as a scratchpad for the state of the Function.
If you delete the metadata collection, all deployed Eventing Functions are undeployed and all associated indexes and constructs are dropped.
note: THE LAST QUOTE IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING: deleting a Function's metadata collection is destructive to every Function using it, cluster-wide, and nothing on the Function's own settings page warns of this - it surfaces only in the terminology glossary. A real operational hazard hiding behind a definitions page.
relates_to_competency_question: Where does a Function keep its own checkpoints and Timer state, and what happens if that storage is deleted?
